For Immediate Release:

November 25, 2026

Ocean Water Use Warning for Los Angeles County Beaches

The Los Angeles County Department of Public Health advises the public to avoid swimming, surfing, and playing in ocean waters at the following Los Angeles County beaches due to elevated bacteria levels that exceed state health standards:

BEACH AREA WARNINGS:

The warning applies to the following locations:

  • Strand Street extensions at Santa Monica Beach

100 yards up and down the coast from Lifeguard Tower #24.

  • Malibu Lagoon at Surfrider Beach

100 yards up and down the coast from the public restrooms.

  • Topanga Canyon Beach in Malibu

100 yards up and down the coast from the lagoon.

  • Santa Monica Pier in Santa Monica

100 yards up and down the coast from the pier.

  • Pico-Kenter storm drain at Santa Monica Beach. Santa Monica South tower 20

100 yards up and down the coast from the storm drain.

  • Windward storm drain at Venice Beach

100 yards up and down the coast from the storm drain.

  • Dockweiler State Beach. Culver Blvd Storm Drain

100 yards up and down the coast from the storm drain.

  • Dockweiler State Beach. Westchester Storm Drain

100 yards up and down the coast from the storm drain.

  • Imperial Highway storm drain at Dockweiler State Beach. Dockweiler Tower 56

100 yards up and down the coast from the storm drain.

  • Hyperion Plant outfall at Dockweiler State Beach

100 yards up and down the coast from the restrooms.

  • 40th Street extension in Manhattan Beach

100 yards up and down the coast from 40th street.

  • Manhattan Beach Pier in Manhattan Beach

100 yards up and down the coast from the pier.

  • Torrance Beach at Malaga Cove. Just north of RAT tower

100 yards up and down the coast from the lifeguard tower.

  • East Malibu Pier

100 yards up and down the coast from the pier.

  • West Malibu Pier

100 yards up and down the coast from the pier.

  • Dewatering Well Location at Latigo Shore Drive

100 yards up and down the coast from the public access steps.

  • Treatment Plant Location at Latigo Shore Drive

100 yards up and down the coast from the public access steps.

  • Solstice Creek at Dan Blocker County Beach

Entire swim area.

  • Mother’s Beach in Marina Del Rey

Entire swim area.

  • Long Point in Rancho Palos Verdes

Entire swim area.

REASON FOR WARNING:

These warnings are issued because recent water samples showed bacterial levels exceeding health standards, which may increase the risk of illness.
